synopsis: Over-fitting means settings fit the tuning tests well but perform worse on new tests; for braking-system release claims, the booklet requires a frozen, stratified random sample from the declared operating-domain distribution, drawn before tuning and never used for tuning [f14306, f14131]. The main controls are grouped holdouts of whole sites, weather episodes, machines or scenario families, separate tuning/validation/untouched audit datasets, and limited frozen-set use at release candidates rather than continuous optimisation against failures [f137, f6990, f6992, f12889, f7135]. Simulator over-fitting is identified as a critical risk, with improving virtual metrics alongside stalled or worsening held-out real performance as its warning sign, but the skeptic’s review found no off-road case and explicitly treats the risk as an inference [f11030, f10784]. Independent withheld physical datasets and blind correlation tests are recommended safeguards; failed tests and discrepancy dispositions should remain visible rather than mismatches being tuned away or scenarios removed from reporting [f11032, f8047, f8024]. Separately, Chapter 5 reports severe over-fitting and poor novel-path generalisation in single-traversal 3DGS, a problem addressed by VEGS in July 2024; this evidence is labelled on-road, not an established off-road braking-function case [f4010, f4011, f10783].
